rulings.ruling: APPROVED. QE-R7AF-01 is closed in my scope. After an unfinished, unreviewed re-entry week, a later break starts from the re-entry plus the executed facts, whatever was decided on Monday of week 6. I probed equipment window, the full-kit statement recorded as KEEP, systemic and local fatigue, and schedule and goal changes. All give the control's start: run step 0, week 6 runs EASY 15 / LONG 20, and a projected week 7 of back-squat 1x5@4 ESTABLISH RETURN_ENTRY with LONG 45. Executed and reviewed from there, the long runs of weeks 6 to 9 are 20/20/25/30, with O 0 and J 0. R7A-FINAL-FREEZE used the unexecuted step 1: week 6 at 30/45, a projected week 7 of 2x5@3 KNOWN 82.5 with LONG 60, and executed long runs of 45/45/50/55. On Sunday of week 5 the week is complete: a review, or a schedule change applying its rule, steps only what was executed (back-squat and calf raise at the 20 kg lifted). The run holds because Thursday's run was missed (byte-equal to R7A-FINAL-FREEZE). A strength-only change on Sunday 06:00 keeps the run start projected, and B starts from the re-entry.

newFindings.finding: historicalWeekStart holds a start as history only when both sports' parts hold, and inside a return 'executed in full' is per week, across sports. So on a re-entry week left without its own review (here, its Sunday session reported on Monday), a strength-only shortfall also returns the run to the entry. A lighter effort-guided load or a missed lift is enough, though every run was executed. S-B lighter: the run repeats its entry (15/20, then 30/30/45, against 30/45, then 34/45/60). The controlled pair differs only in the strength loads. S-D held: two weeks of executed return steps are lost for both sports (long runs 20, then 45/50/55, against 60/60/60/65). The dossier's S-B and S-D rows do not mention the run.
newFindings.whyNotBlocking: It raises no dose and breaks no declared rule. Every output is the approved entry, steps and ceilings from a state the athlete executed (O 0, J 0). It is nonclinical, and it never reaches before the return in force. It needs an unconsolidated re-entry week with a shortfall and another interruption inside the same return. With the re-entry week reviewed, nothing changes (isolation case). It is the declared boundary B8, and the alternative needs per-sport (or per-exercise) authority, which the contract names as a new state model. The cost is progression, not safety: a lower dose that persists costs adaptation (R6-S52).

nonBlockingRecommendations.owner: Runtime author with Product/UX and Data
nonBlockingRecommendations.recommendation: Walk the state point back per sport: the run's point from the run part's authority, and strength's from strength's. Count 'executed in full' per sport inside a return, so a strength shortfall cannot discard executed run steps, nor the reverse. Product/UX and Data should also make sure the re-entry week is consolidated by its own review when its last session is logged late, for example a week-end consolidation that reads late logs. Until then, keep the conservative reading.
